candidate.title: NET-Seq
candidate.scope: The immunoprecipitation-based NET-Seq (native elongating transcript sequencing) workflow in the third row of the assigned Illumina poster crop: RNAPII elongation complex → immunoprecipitated complex → extracted RNA → reverse transcription → cDNA. The leftmost polymerase/RNA cartoon and the caption Native elongating transcript sequencing (NET-Seq) identify the target; they are not an additional preparation step. The visible DeepCAGE, 3′NT method and mNET-seq rows are separately labelled neighboring workflows, not branches of this card. The chemical drawing at the far right has no connecting NET-Seq arrow. This extraction preserves the schematic's broad RNA-to-cDNA block; it does not supply an executable or complete adapter-bearing library protocol. NET-seq is the same name with different capitalization, not a second method. The cited original paper's abstract establishes nascent RNA 3′-end sequencing and a yeast application; no claim is made that every NET-seq implementation uses this capture route.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate complex
operations.description: Capture the input RNAPII elongation complex by immunoprecipitation, retaining polymerase-associated nascent RNA in the selected material. The output differs by antibody-mediated capture of the intact RNA–polymerase association.
operations.mechanism: Immunoprecipitation of the RNAPII complex; the drawing places antibodies on the polymerase, rather than on isolated RNA.
operations.information_effect: Physical association with captured RNAPII enriches the RNA population for nascent polymerase-associated transcripts. Capture is not proof of perfect specificity: the catalogue explicitly warns that nonspecific antibodies can precipitate nonspecific complexes. The cap cartoon is not a cap-selection operation.
